additional_info.subject: Issue Description
additional_info.body: All SicD are not working via Hubject roaming platform. MOL has Driivz as BE. Here is the letter from them: Why the Siemens Sicharge D chargers are pushed with External value for CalibrationLawDataAvailabilityType parameter, Driivz has changed the value in the DB, so the CDRs are now good without the signed meter data. However, if the configuration will be re-uploaded then we will face again this issue, so please answer the two questions below and inform us how you can support us in this final resolution. CalibrationLawDataAvailabilityType = External value is coming from. When a charger sends us a "public key" we mark it as Eichrecht compatible. We receive it as part of the "data transfer" notification. The charger then need to share the signed meter data with us, but in this case it doesn't Hubject is confused and reject our CDR. Driivz is asking why they are getting the public key ? why they do not get the signed meter data at the end of the charge?

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0433413-DC/Si-D/HU-[MP / S3 170003429] All units not functional CRM:02919000032
additional_info.body:
Dear Szilard,
Apologies for the delayed answer. Today I took in charge this ticket
ID0433413
and analyzed the doubts and the questions you reported to us from the End customer.
If I understood correctly your query, the Backend operator is complaining that they are receiving public keys from the chargers, as if they were ERK compliant chargers.
It looks to me that this could be an issue between the Backend and Hubject roaming platform. From your email, you mention:
"
When a charger sends us a "public key" we mark it as Eichrecht compatible. We receive it as part of the "data transfer" notification. The charger then need to share the signed meter data with us
."
All these three statements are correct. However, I checked the 12 chargers at MOL that are online on SCB, and what I found is:
All chargers are not configured as ERK
Over the past 2 month, the chargers never sent any key to the Backend in the BootNotification
Over the past 2 months, the chargers never sent the command "Data Transfer", hence no "publicKey" was sentto the Backend.
Could you clarify what the customer means with the parameter "
CalibrationLawDataAvailabilityType
"? It is not a OCPP Parameter.
The chargers are not sending the signed meter data at the of charging, as they are not configured as ERK.
It looks to me the issue is in the roaming between Hubjet platform and the Backend, hence it is outside of Siemens' responsibilities.
I hope these points above help you to redirect the issue towards the roaming platform and the backend. Please let me know if you require further information, or if I did not reply to all the queries from the end customer. You can call me in the next days if required.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0433413-DC/Si-D/HU-[MP / S3 170003429] All units not functional CRM:02919000032
additional_info.body:
Dear Szilard,
As we discussed today during our call, it is necessary to understand, first from Hubject roaming platform and then from Driivz, what parameters are they receiving (or not receiving) that are causing the issue. As we discussed, Hubject is claiming to receive this parameter "
CalibrationLawDataAvailabilityType"
. However, this is not a OCPP parameter according to the OCPP 1.6 protocol (I attach it to this email for your convenience).
The parameters that the charger exchanges with the Backend can be seen both in the "GetConfiguration" command and in the config file.
I attach to this email the config file of charger "H4Jbpz" and an overview of the GetConfiguration commands sent in the last 2 days from the MOL chargers. As you can see, no parameter is exchanged which refers to Calibration Law Data.
Hence, before proceeding further with any alignment with the providers, it is necessary to understand from where the roaming platform is getting this parameter.
I am looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!
